post.title: Personality Based Matchmaking in Online Courses?
post.body: Feels kinda cool but also tricky to trust AI doing personality checks. SAMI wants to make online study groups better by guessing your personality from forum posts, says this new research on AmbitionBox. For us working or studying online, better matching can mean less awkward team projects and more connected classmates but honestly, I worry if the AI really gets people or just labels them wrong. post.title: LLMs ka decision explain karna itna tough kyun hai?
post.body: Yaar this is getting confusing. Latest news from research says LLMs struggle to explain their own decisions properly, they give explanations that don't really help much. Basically, these language models try to generate minimal changes to explain why they made a choice, but often those small edits don't even affect the outcome. For people like us working with AI or just curious, it kinda feels unreliable, especially if we want clear reasoning behind automated decisions in our projects. Kya aap logon ne kabhi kisi AI tool se aise confusing explanations dekhe hain? How do you handle jab model khud apne decisions samjha nahi pata?
post.source: LLMs Don't Know Their Own Decision Boundaries: The Unreliability of Self-Generated Counterfactual Explanations

original_news.title: CDE: Curiosity-Driven Exploration for Efficient Reinforcement Learning in Large Language Models
original_news.brief: → Curiosity-Driven Exploration (CDE) is introduced as a framework to enhance the exploration ability of Large Language Models (LLMs) in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) paradigm. → CDE utilizes the model's intrinsic curiosity by incorporating signals from both the actor and the critic, using perplexity for the actor and variance of value estimates for the critic as exploration bonuses within the RLVR framework. → Theoretical analysis demonstrates that CDE penalizes overconfident errors and promotes response diversity, while connecting the critic-wise bonus to the count-based exploration bonus in RL. → Empirical results show that CDE achieves around a 3-point improvement over standard RLVR methods on AIME benchmarks, revealing insights into calibration collapse mechanisms in RLVR and common failure modes in LLMs.

post.title: Disentanglement without assuming independence? Interest piqued
post.body: This stuff really messes with how I thought representation learning works. The paper on arxiv says our usual way to separate factors assumes they dont depend on each other, but real life data rarely behaves that way. For people like us working with data models, this means we might be missing out on capturing real patterns just because we expect perfect independence. I wonder if anyone here has tried handling dependent factors in their projects? Would love to hear how it affected your results or if it just made everything more complicated.
